Twenty-five comments

“As I Went Out Upon the Ice”

A member, ‘dubhghaill’, made an inquiry in discussions:

Discussion: West Kerry Polka
# Posted on July 22nd 2007 by dubhghaill
https://thesession.org/discussions/14536

That sent me out looking for polkas from West Kerry, and in particular polkas that began eA ~… I found several, including some melodies that I couldn’t find on site here, though some seem to share the same name and even share parts… I found this, with two different B-parts.

Here are some others on site to compare these two takes with ~

“Tralee Gaol” ~ Also known as: “As I Went Out Upon The Ice”, “Glen Cottage”, “Glen Cottage Polka #2”, “Glen Cottage Polka 2”, “Glen Cottage Polka No.2”, “The Green Cockade”, “The Haughs O‘ Cromdale”, “The Haughs Of Cromdale”, “O’Neill’s March”.
Key signature: G Major
Submitted on November 6th 2002 by alastair wilson.
https://thesession.org/tunes/1113

“The Glen Cottage Polka”
Key signature: E Dorian
Submitted on December 5th 2005 by hetty.
https://thesession.org/tunes/5278

& ~ there is another take also known as “As I Went Out Upon the Ice”, and also beginning eA ~ … :-/

|: eA BA | eA BA | eA BA | ~ It may be different enough to also warrant a place on site, if it isn’t already here in one key or t’other…

As I went out etc.

Same tune, posted by ceolachan, but with extra bits. I have to say I expect him to be generally correct.

Mac, this is a polka so 2/4 time signature with quavers is correct. You have 4/4 but with quavers as the “basic” note length, should be crotchets in 4/4. Doesn’t add up!

Also, the tonality is around A, so the key is not a D key (& not 2 #, either).
Ceolachan’s posting shows 1 #. and A dorian as the key; i.e. A tonality with a G key signature.

All the best

Peter Jenkins

# Posted on September 3rd 2012 by Mac McGrath

↳ Posted by ceolachan on September 3rd, 2012.

“…(& not 2 #, either)….”

There are no Cs or C#s in the tune (in this setting, at least) so it makes no difference to the melody whether or not there is a C# in the key signature. However, if you are using A minor* as an accompanying chord, then the hypothetical C# would clash.

*An A major chord, whilst bringing out a different character in the tune, would not necessarily be incorrect. Leaving out the 3rd of the chord (‘A5’ - consisting of A and E notes only) would allow both possibilities.

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - ~ NOTES ~ - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

“…(& not 2 #, either)….”

There are no Cs or C#s in the tune (in this setting, at least) so it makes no difference to the melody whether or not there is a C# in the key signature. However, if you are using A minor* as an accompanying chord, then the hypothetical C# would clash.

*An A major chord, whilst bringing out a different character in the tune, would not necessarily be incorrect. Leaving out the 3rd of the chord (‘A5’ - consisting of A and E notes only) would allow both possibilities.
